subject: Before changing the mattress, look at the whole night
preheader: A useful equipment brief starts with the night-time routine, not a product code.
intro: A difficult night is not always explained by the mattress alone.
The person's routine, positioning, transfers, assistance, room setup and equipment all shape what happens from getting into bed to getting up again.
sectionTitle: Start with the part of the night that is not working
body: Before narrowing the equipment options, it helps to identify when the difficulty occurs and what the person is trying to do at that point.
That gives a home trial a practical purpose. It also helps separate a comfort question from a positioning, access, transfer or assistance question.
questions: Getting into bed: are height, access or transfers creating the problem?
Through the night: are comfort, positioning or repositioning breaking down?
Getting up: does the setup support the morning transfer and routine?
actionTitle: Have a night-time routine that needs a closer look?
actionText: Tell us about the person's goals, what is not working in their current sleep setup and what needs to improve overnight. We can then help identify the bed, mattress and accessories worth trialling together at home.
boundary: Sleep Choice focuses on the equipment setup and home trial. Any broader sleep or clinical assessment remains with the treating team.
teamName: The Sleep Choice x Supply Ministry Team
trialFooterText: Seven-night in-home trial availability, service area, equipment configuration and individual arrangements are confirmed per case.
